reasons: Both texts use the same frame: an act, then 'he will not find the scent of Paradise, though its scent is found from a distance of N years'.
The act differs completely: A is about killing a man of the protected people (ahl al-dhimma); B is about invoking blessing on the Prophet without his family.
The distance also differs (seventy years in A, five hundred in B). The overlap is a stock warning frame filled with different content, not one report.

reasons: Both say every boy is held in pledge for his aqiqa, slaughtered on the seventh day, his head shaved and he is named.
Differences are minimal wording only: rahin vs murtahan, 'yawm al-sabi' vs 'yawm sabi'ihi', and A adds 'anhu'.

verdicts.uncertainty_note: Both are matn-only fragments without chains; the correspondence rests on the wording, which is near-identical.

reasons: Both have Abu Sa'id al-Khudri telling a man he loves sheep and the desert, instructing him to raise his voice in the call to prayer, because no jinn, human or thing hears the muezzin's voice but will testify for him on the Day of Resurrection, then attributing it to the Prophet.
Variants: B has 'aw' (or) where A has 'wa' (and), 'bil-salat' for 'lil-salat', adds 'bil-nida'' and 'mada' (the reach of the voice).

proposals.text: B adds 'mada' ('the full reach of' the muezzin's voice), so testimony extends to whoever hears it at any distance; A says only 'the voice of the muezzin'.
A says 'in your sheep and your desert'; B says 'in your sheep or your desert'.

reasons: Both contain the Prophet asking the Ansar whether they are not content that people take away worldly goods while they take him to their homes, their answer 'yes', and the saying about the Ansar's mountain path.
A is the full narrative of Hunayn (battle, distribution of spoils, the Ansar's complaint); B gives only the closing exchange.
B differs in wording (ama/ala, 'bi-Muhammad' for 'bi-Rasul Allah', 'diyarikum' for 'buyutikum', 'la-salaktu' for 'la-akhadhtu') and adds an oath and two further sayings not in A.

B adds the oath 'wa-alladhi nafsu Muhammadin bi-yadihi' before the mountain-path saying.
A carries the narrative setting (Hunayn, spoils given to the Muhajirun and the Tulaqa', the Ansar's complaint) that B does not show.

reasons: The only overlap is the shahada ('that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger').
A is a long dialogue on islam, iman, ihsan and the Hour, ending with the questioner identified as Jibril; B is a short ruling on what a woman's iqama consists of.
Their subjects, speakers and contents are otherwise unrelated.

reasons: Both open with the same frame: 'three whom God will not speak to, nor look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify, and theirs is a painful punishment'.

The three named differ entirely: A names an old adulterer, a tyrant king and a proud poor man; B names a man withholding surplus water from the traveller, a man swearing falsely in a sale after 'asr, and a man pledging allegiance to an imam only for worldly gain.
A standard frame filled with different content is not one report.
